distinguishing_features: Engineered micro-pinhole/reentrant cavity surface texture on cooling vessel walls as predefined heterogeneous nucleation sites
Spatial localization of the nucleation event at a deterministic predicted temperature via site geometry (r_s, contact angle)
Application to cryopreservation ice nucleation rather than gas-phase fouling suppression
No additive chemistry; solid-state topographic feature instead of volatile passivant
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to replace stochastic supercooling-burst nucleation with a deterministic, spatially localized ice nucleation event at a predictable temperature so latent heat is released gradually and cell-damaging thermal shock/shear is reduced.
parsed.viable_reason: Micro-pinholed/metastable textured surfaces are a physically sound and manufacturable means (laser etching) to control heterogeneous nucleation onset, and the test is readily runnable with existing freezer thermocouples.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Although the contact-angle nucleation-barrier physics is shared with the halogen-passivation prior art, repurposing engineered topographic nucleation sites (rather than suppressing an additive) to deterministically pin and localize ice nucleation in a cryovial is a non-routine step toward the stated problem.
